title: The Pair Test - a computerised measure of learning and memory
author: Sarah Buck
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bjvckn2w

steps.title: Prepare Equipment and Software
steps.instruction: Set up the necessary hardware and software for the test administration.

substeps.instruction: Obtain an Android tablet (Apple devices are not compatible).
Download the Pair Test application from GooglePlay.
Ensure the device volume is on to facilitate the Spoken Words subtest.
Prepare the 'Pair Test_Record form' for scoring.

steps.title: Initialize Application
steps.instruction: Start the application and identify the participant.

substeps.instruction: Enter the participant's ID (images will be saved on the device with this ID as a prefix).
Click 'Play'.

steps.title: Provide General Instructions
steps.instruction: Explain the overall nature of the five memory tests to the participant.

substeps.instruction: Inform the participant they will complete five memory tests involving pairs of words, objects, shapes, or made-up words.
Advise them to try their best regardless of difficulty.

steps.title: Administer Task Learning Phase
steps.instruction: Execute the encoding and cued recall cycles for each of the five tasks (Auditory words, Visual words, Abstract designs, Objects, and Pseudowords).

substeps.instruction: Provide task-specific instructions: show an example and explain that they will see/hear 10 pairs, click their preferred item in each pair, and later try to recall the paired item by writing, drawing, or saying it.
Perform the Encoding phase: Present 10 pairs individually for 5 seconds each; the participant must click the stimulus they prefer.

Perform the Cued Recall phase: Present the left-side stimulus of each pair; the participant must provide the associate (say out loud for auditory words, write on canvas for written words/pseudowords, or draw on canvas for objects/designs).
Repeat the Encoding and Cued Recall cycle 3 times in a row for the task to establish a learning curve.
Between Trial 1 and 2, instruct: 'We will do the same thing again, with the same pairs but in a different order. Again, for each pair click on the one you prefer.'
After Trial 3, instruct: 'I want you to keep these pairs in memory because I will ask you to remember as many as you can in about 15 minutes. In the meantime, we will start another game.'
Do not provide feedback on performance during these trials.

steps.title: Manage Task Order and Timing
steps.instruction: Coordinate the administration of the five tasks to avoid interference and manage the 15-minute delay.

substeps.instruction: Alternate between verbal and non-verbal materials.
Record the exact time the learning phase finishes for each task in the 'time' table.
Note that encoding for a second task can be performed during the 15-minute delay period of the first task.

steps.title: Administer Delayed Recall
steps.instruction: Test the participant's memory after the required interval.

substeps.instruction: Wait exactly 15 minutes after the end of the learning trials for that specific task; if 15 minutes have not passed, provide a small break.
Instruct: 'Now we are going to go back to the [words/pseudowords/shapes/objects] from before. Can you try and remember as many pairs as you can?'

steps.title: Administer Recognition Task
steps.instruction: Perform the forced-choice recognition task immediately following the delayed recall.

substeps.instruction: For standard tasks: Present the cue (first stimulus) and instruct the participant to select the target associate from 3 choices.
For auditory words: Instruct the participant to click each fish to hear the 3 possibilities, then click and hold the fish to select the answer (a 'bip' sound indicates the move to the next pair).

steps.title: Score Performance
steps.instruction: Evaluate the participant's responses using the answer sheets (Version A or B).

substeps.instruction: Categorize each answer as Correct or Incorrect.
Classify incorrect answers into 5 types: DK (no answer), Semantic (related meaning), Form (looks/sounds similar), From list (another item from the list), or Other (invented item).
Calculate the average learning score by averaging the three learning trials for each task.
Transfer the number of errors into the 'types of errors' table in the record form.

steps.title: Calculate Composite and Standard Scores
steps.instruction: Convert raw data into standardized metrics.

substeps.instruction: Calculate raw scores for Learning (average of 3 trials), Delayed Recall (score at recall), and Delayed Recognition (Correct responses minus Familiar and New errors: C-F-N).
Multiply these raw scores by 10 to obtain composite scores.

Calculate general composite scores: General Learning/Recall (average of general learning and general recall composite scores), General Recognition (box C), and General Memory (average of general learning, general recall, and general recognition composite scores).
Convert all composite scores to standard scores using the provided standardization tables.
